title: The Investigating Tactile Experiences and Textures with Sustainable Materials in Art and Design Education
research_question: This study aims: (1) to explore tactile experiences with various sustainable materials, including those sourced from seashell waste, eggshell waste, and Jesmonite; (2) to examine these materials through experiential learning practices to discover their potential in enhancing the creative process; and (3) to measure students' agreement using a questionnaire on tactile experiences with sustainable materials in educational settings, thereby promoting a participatory and tactile-focused learning approach.

participants.description: 48 student participants (42% male, 58% female) from Dhurakij Pundit University and Bangkok Design Week. The majority (54%) were below 20 years old, 40% were 20-25 years old, and 6% were 25 and above. 94% had college education, 6% had education beyond college. Academic disciplines were primarily Art (54.17%) and Design (35.42%), with 10.42% from other fields.
participants.recruitment: Participants were recruited from Dhurakij Pundit University (45 students) for workshops on January 15-16, 2024, and from Bangkok Design Week (3 graduate students) for a workshop on February 3, 2024.

stimuli_or_exposures.description: Sustainable materials including Jesmonite, seashell waste, eggshell waste, coffee bean grounds, stucco, rice husk, bamboo fiber, and small natural pebbles were used in hands-on workshops to create diverse tactile textures.

Participatory workshops were conducted in environments conducive to experiential learning, tactile experience engagement, and detailed discussions at Dhurakij Pundit University and SUPH Art Space during Bangkok Design Week.

mechanisms: Tactile experiences are not merely sensory but also intertwined with emotions and social interactions, providing insight into the material nature of surroundings.
Experiential learning, particularly through participatory workshops, is a transformative process where knowledge is derived from active and emotional engagement with materials.
Sustainable materials offer unique sensory experiences that challenge conventional perceptions and encourage innovative thinking, fostering creativity.
Students recognize the critical importance of tactile elements (textures) and the value of sustainable materials for environmental and community well-being.
implementation_implications: Educational institutions, especially in art and design, should incorporate tactile experiences with sustainable materials into curricula through participatory workshops, hands-on sessions, and project-based learning.
Further research is needed into the psychological and emotional effects of tactile interaction with sustainable materials to enhance educational strategies.

Exploring digital and virtual reality technologies to simulate tactile experiences with sustainable materials could extend experiential learning to long-distance learners and provide scalable solutions.
Integrating tactile experiences with sustainable materials into art and design education is valuable for deepening understanding and promoting sustainable practices.
